explanation: Human age distribution is split into prereproductive, reproductive, and postreproductive groups. MDCs and LDCs exhibit highly distinct age structure diagrams. Many MDCs possess a stable age structure. In contrast, most LDCs have a youthful age profile and are experiencing rapid population growth. Due to this youthful profile, even if LDCs immediately reduced birth rates to 2 children per family (replacement level), the population would continue to grow for some time (a phenomenon known as population momentum).

questions.q: Why would reducing births to 2 children per family in Less-Developed Countries (LDCs) still result in population growth?
opts: Because LDCs have a highly stable age structure.
Because LDCs have a youthful age profile, which ensures continued growth as children enter reproductive age.
Because MDCs would begin migrating to LDCs in large numbers.
Because LDCs have higher postreproductive survival rates than MDCs.
questions.exp: The notes state that 'Even reducing births to 2 per family in LDC would result in population growth because of age profile' referring to their 'youthful profile.'
